reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. Write H_j for the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree j, with its integer coefficients interpreted in R (H_0(t)=1, H_1(t)=t, and H_(n+1)(t)=t H_n(t)-n H_(n-1)(t) for n>=1). Define Phi_j(w)=[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)] in L^2(gamma_E; R), where brackets denote the almost-everywhere equivalence class of the literal square-integrable function displayed. For every finite subset s of N={0,1,2,...} and every coefficient sequence c:N -> R, define F_(s,c):E -> L^2(gamma_E; R) by F_(s,c)(w)=sum_(j in s) c(j) Phi_j(w). Then F_(s,c) is twice continuously Frechet differentiable over R on the entire ambient space E, with derivatives taken with respect to w in the L^2 norm. There is no restriction on the coefficients, and the finite set may be empty.
objects: The finite Hermite feature map F_(s,c)(w)=sum_(j in s) c(j)[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)].
domains: s finite subset of N; c any N -> R; w in all E; codomain L^2(gamma_E; R).
quantifiers: For every E, every finite s and every real sequence c, F_(s,c) is C^2 on E.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product structure with Borel sigma-algebra and finiteness of s only; no summability condition on c.
conclusion: ContDiff R 2 F_(s,c), namely twice continuously Frechet differentiable over R globally in the ambient parameter.
scopes: Regularity holds on all E, not just unit vectors; codomain is the actual L^2 quotient. Only the parameter w is differentiated.
constant_dependencies: The map depends on E,s,c restricted to s. No derivative bounds or auxiliary constants are stated.
semantic_notes: The coefficient sequence is held fixed when differentiating the map.
This is a finite sum, without any infinite-series convergence claim.
